Drama is the heavyweight division of ideological filmmaking. Action movies can thrill you into agreement. Comedies can laugh you into acceptance. Horror can frighten you into a worldview. But drama is the genre that sits you down, looks you in the eye, and tells you what to believe about the world for two hours straight. It is the genre of prestige, of Oscars, of Important Conversations. When Hollywood wants to change how you think, it makes a drama. When it wants those convictions to feel earned rather than injected, it wraps them in beautiful cinematography and career-best performances and a score that swells at exactly the right moment to tell you what to feel.

This is not a conspiracy. It is craft. The best filmmakers in the world work in drama, and many of them hold political views far to the left of the audiences who buy tickets. They are not hiding this. They are being celebrated for it. The Palme d'Or, the Golden Lion, the Academy Award for Best Picture -- these are not handed out for ideological neutrality. They are handed out for films that say something, and in 2026, what they say is almost always progressive. The question for parents is not whether these films have a point of view. They all do. The question is whether you know what that point of view is before you sit down with your family.

The numbers tell the story. VirtueVigil has now reviewed 283 drama films and shows -- 235 of them movies. That is more than any other genre in our database by a significant margin. Within those 235 drama films, the ideological distribution is striking: the genre's average woke score runs substantially ahead of its traditional score, and of the 20 most ideologically aggressive drama movies, 16 carry a WOKE verdict, three of which hit STRONGLY WOKE. Only one -- Parasite, at #20 -- drops to WOKE LEAN. Drama is not just Hollywood's most important genre. It is also, by the data, its most reliably progressive one.

This list ranks the 20 most woke drama films we have ever scored, from most ideologically aggressive to least. Each entry links to the full VirtueVigil review with complete scoring methodology, content warnings, and parental guidance. Rankings are determined by VirtueVigil's dual-metric system: Traditional Score measures traditional values present, Woke Score measures progressive ideological content, and Margin is the gap. If drama is the genre that builds your family's moral imagination, you should know what these 20 films are building.

#1 (Most Woke): Anora (2024)

STRONGLY WOKE TRAD: 9.9 WOKE: 35.8 MARGIN: +25.9 WOKE

Genre: Drama • Director: Sean Baker • Cast: Mikey Madison, Yura Borisov, Mark Eydelshteyn, Karren Karagulian • Year: 2024

Hollywood handed its highest honor -- Best Picture at the 97th Academy Awards -- to a film whose protagonist is a sex worker and exotic dancer, whose marriage to a Russian oligarch's son is treated as aspirational, and whose climactic act of self-discovery involves rejecting every traditional institution that supposedly failed her. Sean Baker's film is brilliantly made. Mikey Madison's performance is a star-making turn. The craft is undeniable. But the moral architecture is built on the proposition that Ani's pre-existing life as a strip-club worker is not just her circumstance but her authentic identity, and that the only real violence in the film is anyone who tries to take her away from it. At +25.9, Anora is the most woke drama in the VirtueVigil database by a meaningful margin. It is the Best Picture winner. It is what Hollywood believes in right now. Parents should know this is an R-rated film with graphic sexual content, and the ideology is baked into the premise, not sprinkled on top.

#2: Emilia Perez (2024)

STRONGLY WOKE TRAD: 5.0 WOKE: 30.4 MARGIN: +25.4 WOKE

Genre: Musical / Crime / Drama • Director: Jacques Audiard • Cast: Zoe Saldana, Karla Sofia Gascon, Selena Gomez, Adriana Paz • Platform: Netflix • Year: 2024

Emilia Perez managed the rare feat of uniting both progressive and conservative critics against it while simultaneously earning 13 Oscar nominations -- the most for any non-English-language film in Academy history. The transgender cartel musical won Best Supporting Actress (Zoe Saldana) and Best Original Song. What unifies the criticism from both sides is the same thing that makes the film so ideologically revealing: it is not a film about a transgender woman who happens to be a cartel boss. It is a film that uses a cartel boss's gender transition as a redemption arc, arguing through its musical numbers and its narrative structure that the real crime was not the drug trafficking but the performance of masculinity that preceded it. At +25.4 woke margin with a near-zero 5.0 traditional score, this is one of the most ideologically lopsided films in the entire database. The traditional score is submerged so thoroughly that the film essentially has no countervailing values content whatsoever. Parents should know this is a Netflix original available to anyone with an account, and the 13 Oscar nominations mean it will surface in every algorithm for years.

#3: Hamlet (2026)

STRONGLY WOKE TRAD: 9.0 WOKE: 30.2 MARGIN: +21.3 WOKE

Genre: Drama / Tragedy • Director: Aneil Karia • Cast: Riz Ahmed, Art Malik, Sheeba Chaddha, Morfydd Clark, Joe Alwyn, Timothy Spall • Year: 2026

Aneil Karia's reimagining of Shakespeare's greatest tragedy transposes the Danish court to a modern South Asian diaspora context, with Riz Ahmed as a Prince Hamlet whose paralysis is not existential but systemic. The film argues that Hamlet's famous indecision is not a character flaw but a rational response to a world where institutions -- family, state, religion -- have already failed him. The traditional reading of Hamlet as a meditation on mortality, justice, and the burden of moral action is reconfigured here as a study in institutional betrayal. The 30.2 woke score reflects a production where nearly every structural choice serves a progressive reading of the text: the court is corrupt beyond redemption, the ghost is an unreliable narrator from a colonized lineage, and Ophelia's madness is reworked as political awakening rather than personal collapse. At +21.3, this is the most ideologically aggressive Shakespeare adaptation we have reviewed. Parents should know the language is Shakespearean but the politics are 2026.

#4: Midsommar (2019)

WOKE TRAD: 2.4 WOKE: 20.6 MARGIN: +18.2 WOKE

Genre: Horror / Drama • Director: Ari Aster • Cast: Florence Pugh, Jack Reynor, Vilhelm Blomgren, William Jackson Harper • Year: 2019

Midsommar is a genuinely good film. That is the most important thing to say before everything else, because it shapes how dangerous it is. If Midsommar were a crude feminist horror film, if the cult were obviously evil from the first scene and the protagonist's eventual participation were clearly framed as tragedy, it would be less ideologically effective. Instead, Ari Aster constructs a slow-motion argument that the pagan commune at the center of the film -- the one that performs ritual suicide, blood-eagles a man, and drugs unwitting visitors -- is healthier for its female protagonist than her American relationship. Christian (Jack Reynor) is a bad boyfriend. The film makes this case so thoroughly, and his betrayals feel so earned, that by the time Dani (Florence Pugh) participates in his ritual murder, the audience has been conditioned to feel relief. The 2.4 traditional score is among the lowest on this list. There is effectively no countervailing moral framework. The cult's atrocities are real but the film's sympathies are entirely with Dani, and Dani's arc ends with her smiling into the camera as her boyfriend burns alive inside a bear carcass. Parents should know this is not a date-night horror movie. It is a feminist revenge fantasy wrapped in daylight and flowers.

#5: A Different Man (2024)

WOKE TRAD: 0.0 WOKE: 17.6 MARGIN: +17.6 WOKE

Genre: Thriller / Drama / Sci-Fi • Director: Aaron Schimberg • Cast: Sebastian Stan, Adam Pearson, Renate Reinsve • Year: 2024

A Different Man is a woke trap in the most literal sense. The film presents as an indie character study about an actor with neurofibromatosis who undergoes an experimental treatment that gives him a conventionally attractive face. The surface argument is about self-acceptance and the shallowness of physical beauty. The actual argument, which emerges with brutal clarity by the third act, is that male entitlement, romantic rejection, and violent revenge are the inevitable outcomes of giving a socially marginal man access to the privileges of the conventionally attractive. Edward's transformation does not liberate him. It reveals him. And what it reveals, according to the film, is a toxic entitlement that was always there. At 0.0, A Different Man has the lowest traditional score in the entire VirtueVigil database -- literally zero measurable traditional values content. At +17.6 woke margin, it stands as one of the most ideologically pure progressive dramas we have ever reviewed. Parents should know this is not a feel-good story about overcoming adversity. It is an indictment of male desire disguised as a character study.

#6: Mother Mary (2025)

WOKE TRAD: 6.4 WOKE: 23.7 MARGIN: +17.3 WOKE

Genre: Psychological Drama / Thriller / Music • Director: David Lowery • Cast: Anne Hathaway, Michaela Coel, Hunter Schafer, FKA Twigs • Year: 2025

David Lowery's first major engagement with the machinery of celebrity and pop music emerges as a film about power, intimacy, and the cost of being watched. Anne Hathaway plays Mother Mary, an iconic pop star whose career has been built on image, control, and the careful management of what the public is allowed to see. The film treats celebrity as a system of oppression, the pop industrial complex as a machine that consumes women, the male gaze as a form of violence, and female intimacy as the only authentic refuge from a world designed by and for men. The 23.7 woke score reflects a film where every relationship, every power dynamic, and every creative choice is filtered through an ideological lens that treats traditional institutions -- marriage, the music industry, the church (the title is not accidental) -- as structures of control that women must escape. Parents should know this is A24 prestige filmmaking at its most polished and persuasive.

#7: Babygirl (2024)

WOKE TRAD: 4.4 WOKE: 19.2 MARGIN: +14.8 WOKE

Genre: Erotic Thriller / Drama • Director: Halina Reijn • Cast: Nicole Kidman, Harris Dickinson, Antonio Banderas, Sophie Wilde • Platform: Theatrical / A24 • Year: 2024

Babygirl is a well-made, beautifully shot, expertly performed film built around an argument most traditional viewers will find deeply objectionable. It is not a film to dismiss. It is a film to understand before dismissing. Romy Mathis (Nicole Kidman) runs a robotics company in New York. She is successful, married, a mother. She is also profoundly unfulfilled in ways that her husband (Antonio Banderas) cannot reach. Enter Samuel (Harris Dickinson), an intern half her age who sees through her professional armor and offers her a version of intimacy her marriage never provided -- specifically, a BDSM dynamic in which she is the submissive. The film's argument is that Romy's affair is not a betrayal but a liberation, that her marriage was the lie and her submission to Samuel is the truth. At +14.8 woke margin with a 4.4 traditional score, Babygirl is an erotic thriller that treats traditional marriage as a performance and sexual transgression as authenticity. Parents should know this is an R-rated film with explicit sexual content, and the ideology is the premise.

#8: The Apprentice (2024)

WOKE TRAD: 6.6 WOKE: 21.0 MARGIN: +14.4 WOKE

Genre: Biographical Drama • Director: Ali Abbasi • Cast: Sebastian Stan, Jeremy Strong, Maria Bakalova • Platform: Theatrical (Briarcliff Entertainment) • Year: 2024

There is something fascinating about The Apprentice, and it is not what its makers intended. Ali Abbasi and Gabriel Sherman set out to make a Trump origin story that explains the 45th and 47th president as a creation of Roy Cohn -- the ruthless attorney who taught Trump that winning is everything, that admitting defeat is weakness, and that the rules apply only to people who follow them. The film wants you to see Trump as Cohn's monster. What it accidentally reveals is that Cohn's principles -- aggression, loyalty, refusal to apologize -- are the principles that made Trump successful in a world where everyone else was playing by rules they imposed on themselves. Jeremy Strong gives a mesmerizing performance as Cohn, and Sebastian Stan's Trump is more impersonation than inhabitation but functional enough to carry the argument. At +14.4 woke margin, the film is an ideological prosecution dressed as a biopic. Parents should know this is rated R for sexual content, drug use, and language, and it is an election-year political weapon, not a neutral portrait.

#9: The Drama (2026)

WOKE TRAD: 8.4 WOKE: 22.7 MARGIN: +14.2 WOKE

Genre: Dark Comedy / Romance / Drama • Director: Kristoffer Borgli • Cast: Zendaya, Robert Pattinson, Alana Haim, Mamoudou Athie, Hailey Gates • Year: 2026

Kristoffer Borgli, the Norwegian provocateur behind Dream Scenario, has made a film with a single devastating premise: what happens when you discover the person you love once planned to murder children at their school? The answer, across 108 minutes, is that you forgive them. The Drama uses this premise to argue that love demands the suspension of moral judgment, that the past is never as simple as we want it to be, and that holding people accountable for their worst moments is its own form of violence. Zendaya and Robert Pattinson give career-level performances as a couple whose engagement is upended by the discovery of a school-shooting plan from Pattinson's character's adolescence. The 22.7 woke score reflects a film that weaponizes empathy against judgment and treats the act of condemnation as more morally suspect than the act that provoked it. At +14.2 woke margin, this is Borgli's most ideologically aggressive film. Parents should know the subject matter involves school violence, and the film's argument will make many viewers deeply uncomfortable for reasons the film itself does not anticipate.

#10: Nightbitch (2026)

WOKE TRAD: 0.0 WOKE: 14.0 MARGIN: +14.0 WOKE

Genre: Drama • Platform: Hulu • Year: 2026

Nightbitch opens as a character study of maternal exhaustion -- a woman losing her identity in the repetitive isolation of full-time parenthood. The performances are grounded. The frustration feels earned. For roughly the first half of the film, this appears to be a genuine exploration of a universal struggle. Then the transformation begins. The protagonist starts exhibiting canine behavior. She grows fur. She runs with a pack of neighborhood dogs at night. And the film's argument shifts from "motherhood is hard" to "motherhood is a form of dehumanization from which only primal, animal reversion can liberate you." At 0.0 traditional score, Nightbitch joins A Different Man as one of only two films on this list with literally zero measurable traditional values content. The 14.0 woke score reflects a film that treats domesticity as a trap and animal regression as liberation. Parents should know this is a Hulu original, accessible to anyone with a streaming account, and the body-horror elements are genuinely disturbing.

#11: Queer (2024)

WOKE TRAD: 4.2 WOKE: 17.5 MARGIN: +13.3 WOKE

Genre: Romantic Drama • Director: Luca Guadagnino • Cast: Daniel Craig, Drew Starkey, Jason Schwartzman • Platform: Theatrical (A24) • Year: 2024

Daniel Craig gives the best performance of his career in a film that probably should not work as well as it does. Queer is an adaptation of William S. Burroughs' autobiographical novella about his time in 1950s Mexico City, where he lived as an American expatriate, drank heavily, used heroin, and fell into obsessive love with a younger man. Luca Guadagnino treats this material with the same sensual seriousness he brought to Call Me By Your Name, and Craig's performance is so committed that you forget you are watching James Bond. The film's ideology is woven into its aesthetic: the same-sex relationship is rendered with the visual grammar of classic Hollywood romance, effectively arguing through its direction that this is a love story equal to any heterosexual romance ever filmed. At +13.3 woke margin, Queer is less ideologically aggressive than several films below it on this list, but the craft is so persuasive that the argument lands harder. Parents should know this is an R-rated film with explicit sexual content, drug use, and graphic depictions of heroin withdrawal.

#12: Nickel Boys (2024)

WOKE TRAD: 8.7 WOKE: 21.8 MARGIN: +13.1 WOKE

Genre: Drama • Director: RaMell Ross • Cast: Ethan Herisse, Brandon Wilson, Aunjanue Ellis-Taylor, Hamish Linklater, Daveed Diggs • Platform: Theatrical (Orion Pictures / Amazon MGM Studios) • Year: 2024

RaMell Ross has made a film that does not want you to watch it. It wants you to live inside it. Nickel Boys adapts Colson Whitehead's Pulitzer Prize-winning novel about Elwood Curtis, an earnest, idealistic Black teenager in 1960s Tallahassee who is wrongfully sent to Nickel Academy, a fictional reform school based on the real Dozier School for Boys. Ross shoots the entire film in first-person POV -- you see through Elwood's eyes, hear through his ears, experience the casual brutality, the stolen moments of friendship, and the slow erosion of hope as if they are happening to you. The formal innovation is breathtaking. It also makes the film's ideological argument inescapable. You cannot get critical distance from Nickel Boys because Ross has designed the film to deny you that distance. The 21.8 woke score reflects a work where the American carceral system is not analyzed but inhabited, and where the injustice is presented not as historical artifact but as ongoing wound. At +13.1 woke margin, this is one of the most formally ambitious films of 2024 and one of the most ideologically focused.

#13: Girls Like Girls (2026)

WOKE TRAD: 4.2 WOKE: 16.8 MARGIN: +12.6 WOKE

Genre: Romance / Coming-of-Age / Drama • Director: Hayley Kiyoko • Cast: Maya da Costa, Myra Molloy, Levon Hawke, Zach Braff • Year: 2026

Girls Like Girls is exactly what it advertises itself to be. That is both its most honest quality and, for VirtueVigil readers, its most important characteristic to understand upfront. Hayley Kiyoko built a decade of her career on this story -- the 2015 song, the music video, the 2023 novel, now the film -- and she has been consistent throughout: a coming-of-age romance between two teenage girls in which the traditional world (parents, religion, small-town expectations) is the antagonist and the same-sex relationship is the path to authentic selfhood. The 16.8 woke score comes not from formal innovation or narrative complexity but from ideological purity -- every frame of this film knows what it believes and every character exists to advance or obstruct that belief. The 4.2 traditional score reflects the near-total absence of any countervailing perspective. Parents should know this is a YA-aimed film that will arrive looking like a sweet romance and deliver a sustained argument about sexual identity as the core of personhood.

#14: Megalopolis (2024)

WOKE TRAD: 9.0 WOKE: 20.8 MARGIN: +11.8 WOKE

Genre: Epic / Science Fiction / Political Drama • Director: Francis Ford Coppola • Cast: Adam Driver, Giancarlo Esposito, Nathalie Emmanuel, Aubrey Plaza, Shia LaBeouf, Jon Voight, Dustin Hoffman • Platform: Theatrical / VOD • Year: 2024

Here is the thing about Megalopolis that most critics got wrong in both directions: it is not a failure of craft. Francis Ford Coppola knows how to direct. Adam Driver gives a genuinely magnetic performance. The production design, the score, the sheer scale of ambition -- all of it is the work of a master who spent $120 million of his own money because he believed in what he was making. The problem is what he believed. Megalopolis is a progressive utopian fable in which the future of civilization depends on visionary elites overthrowing the constraints of tradition, democracy, and the unenlightened masses. Cesar Catilina (Driver) is an architect-genius who can stop time and wants to build a perfect city. Mayor Cicero (Esposito) is the populist obstructionist who represents everything holding humanity back. The 20.8 woke score reflects a film where the argument is that genius should govern, tradition is a cage, and the masses need to be saved from their own instincts. At +11.8, Megalopolis is the most expensive independent film ever made and one of the most nakedly ideological. Parents should know this is a deeply strange film, not a conventional blockbuster.

#15: Mother Mary (2026)

WOKE TRAD: 7.9 WOKE: 18.8 MARGIN: +10.9 WOKE

Genre: Psychological Drama / Thriller • Director: David Lowery • Cast: Anne Hathaway, Michaela Coel, Hunter Schafer, FKA Twigs • Platform: Theatrical (A24) • Year: 2026

A24 has made a David Lowery psychological thriller about two women who used to be everything to each other, the long silence that followed, and what happens when the pop star calls the costume designer back into her orbit because she needs something only the designer can make. The film's treatment of intimacy between women is the entire text: the central relationship is rendered with the visual grammar of epic romance while the film's male characters exist only as obstacles, threats, or functional props. The title's religious echo is deliberate -- the film positions its protagonist as a secular saint whose suffering at the hands of the industry and her own fame is a form of passion. At +10.9 woke margin, this is a more polished and controlled version of the ideological arguments present in the 2025 Mother Mary, but the tradeoff is that the polish makes the politics harder to see. Parents should know this is prestige filmmaking designed to feel like art while functioning as argument.

#16: Is God Is (2026)

WOKE TRAD: 7.2 WOKE: 17.6 MARGIN: +10.4 WOKE

Genre: Thriller / Drama / Revenge • Director: Aleshea Harris • Cast: Kara Young, Mallori Johnson, Sterling K. Brown, Vivica A. Fox, Janelle Monae, Erika Alexander • Year: 2026

Is God Is is one of the most explicitly ideological films of 2026. Director Aleshea Harris has been clear about what she is making: a Black feminist revenge myth, a film about women's violent agency against a patriarch who destroyed their family. The stylized character names -- Racine the Rough One, Anaia the Quiet One -- announce that this is mythology, not realism. The twin sisters at the center of the film receive a letter from their dying mother commanding them to kill the father who burned them as children. The 17.6 woke score reflects a work where feminine violence is sacred, paternal authority is a death sentence, and the film's moral gravity is entirely on the side of retribution. At +10.4 woke margin, this is revenge cinema in which the revenge is framed as justice and the justice is framed as feminist theology. Sterling K. Brown plays the father with a terrifying magnetism. Parents should know this is a violent film with a body count, and the ideology is the premise.

#17: Priscilla (2023)

WOKE TRAD: 1.5 WOKE: 11.6 MARGIN: +10.1 WOKE

Genre: Biography / Drama • Director: Sofia Coppola • Cast: Cailee Spaeny, Jacob Elordi, Ari Cohen, Dagmara Dominczyk • Year: 2023

Sofia Coppola is one of the most consistent directors working in American cinema. Consistent in craft. Consistent in worldview. And in Priscilla, consistent in producing a film that is both genuinely beautiful and ideologically predictable. The film adapts Priscilla Presley's memoir to tell the story of her relationship with Elvis from her perspective -- specifically, the perspective of a 14-year-old girl courted by the most famous man in the world. Coppola shoots this not as a fairy tale but as a slow-motion gothic imprisonment. Elvis is not a monster. He is worse: he is a man so thoroughly insulated by fame and entitlement that he cannot see the damage he is doing. The 1.5 traditional score is among the lowest on this list, reflecting a film where patriarchy, celebrity, and male desire are presented as a single interlocking system of control. At +10.1 woke margin, Priscilla is Coppola's most politically focused film since The Beguiled. Parents should know this is an R-rated drama about a teenager being groomed by an adult man, and the film does not flinch from that framing.

#18: Wuthering Heights (2026)

WOKE TRAD: 26.0 WOKE: 36.0 MARGIN: +10.0 WOKE

Genre: Drama • Director: Emerald Fennell • Cast: Margot Robbie, Jacob Elordi, Hong Chau • Year: 2026

Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights survived 179 years, multiple adaptations, and the entire twentieth century with its reputation intact. Heathcliff and Cathy remain two of literature's most electrically rendered figures -- wild, selfish, cosmically intertwined, and ultimately destroyed by the gap between what they want and what society permits. Emerald Fennell's adaptation is the first to explicitly cast Heathcliff as a character of color (Jacob Elordi) and to foreground the novel's racial subtext as the primary engine of its tragedy. This choice is not a gimmick. It is a reading. Fennell argues that Heathcliff's otherness is the novel's central motor, and she builds the entire adaptation around the proposition that Wuthering Heights is not a love story but a study in how systemic racism corrupts every relationship it touches. At +10.0 woke margin with a rare combination of high traditional (26.0) AND high woke (36.0) scores, this is an ideologically complex film -- one of the few on this list that contains substantial traditional content alongside its progressive argument. The high traditional score reflects the source material's enduring moral gravity. The even higher woke score reflects what Fennell did with it. Parents should know this is a period drama with contemporary politics, and the violence is emotional as much as physical.

#19: The Last Witness (2026)

WOKE TRAD: 4.5 WOKE: 14.4 MARGIN: +9.9 WOKE

Genre: Legal Thriller / Drama • Director: Greta Gerwig • Cast: Saoirse Ronan, Bradley Cooper, Toni Collette, Oscar Isaac, Anna Kendrick • Year: 2026

Greta Gerwig returns to the director's chair with a legal thriller that uses the courtroom as a stage for prosecuting institutional failures. Saoirse Ronan plays a journalist who becomes the last living witness to a corporate cover-up with fatal consequences, and Bradley Cooper plays the attorney whose loyalties shift as the trial forces him to choose between his career and his conscience. The 14.4 woke score reflects a film where corporations are inherently corrupt, the legal system is a tool of the powerful, and individual conscience is the only meaningful counterforce to institutional evil. The 4.5 traditional score reflects the near-total absence of any institutional trust. At +9.9 woke margin, The Last Witness is Gerwig operating in genre mode with the same ideological commitments she brought to Barbie. Parents should know this is a legal thriller with adult themes, and the politics are what you would expect from Gerwig -- just delivered through cross-examination instead of monologue.

#20: Parasite (2019)

WOKE LEAN TRAD: 7.8 WOKE: 16.5 MARGIN: +8.7 WOKE

Genre: Thriller / Dark Comedy / Drama • Director: Bong Joon-ho • Cast: Song Kang-ho, Choi Woo-shik, Park So-dam, Chang Hyae-jin, Lee Sun-kyun • Year: 2019

Parasite is a masterfully made film. Let us get that out of the way immediately. Bong Joon-ho is a technical virtuoso. The script architecture is near-perfect. The performances are uniformly excellent. The tonal shifts, from dark comedy to thriller to tragedy, are executed with a confidence that most directors spend careers trying to achieve once and Bong manages multiple times in two hours. It won the Palme d'Or and Best Picture for reasons that have nothing to do with politics. But the politics are there, and they are not subtle. The Kim family lives in a semi-basement apartment, folding pizza boxes for cash. The Park family lives in a modernist mansion designed by a famous architect. The film's central argument is that the barrier between these two worlds is structural, not personal -- that the Kims are not poor because of individual failures but because the system is designed to keep them poor while the Parks benefit from their labor without ever seeing them as human. At +8.7 woke margin, Parasite is the least ideologically aggressive film on this list, and that is precisely what makes it the most effective. Bong does not lecture. He builds a clockwork of class resentment, winds it tight, and lets it explode. Parents should know this is an R-rated film in Korean with English subtitles, with violence and adult themes. It is also one of the best films of the 21st century, and that combination -- genius craft plus progressive politics -- is exactly why drama remains Hollywood's most powerful ideological weapon.
